subject: Hospitality
title: Occupancy Rate: Filling the House
description: A micro-lesson that makes Occupancy Rate: Filling the House usable.

hook.text: Occupancy rate measures what percentage of available rooms are sold. Simple in concept, critical in practice.

buildup.text: Occupancy = Rooms Sold ÷ Total Available Rooms. If 90 of 100 rooms are sold, occupancy is 90%. The goal is rarely 100%.

discovery.text: Most hotels target 70–85% occupancy. Hitting 100% means you probably priced too low—you left money on the table.

twist.text: Full occupancy strains housekeeping, raises costs, and reduces service quality. Sometimes 85% is more profitable than 100%.

climax.text: Revenue managers optimize the blend: high enough occupancy to spread fixed costs, not so high that margins suffer.

punchline.text: 100% full isn't the goal. The right occupancy maximizes profit, not headcount.

quiz.question: Why isn't 100% occupancy always the goal for hotels?
options: It strains operations and may mean rooms were priced too low
